Project Overview
This project explores the relationship between playing time (minutes) and statistical output across both the WNBA and NBA for the 2025–2026 seasons.

Data Sources:

WNBA: SportsDataverse (wehoop)
NBA: ESPN (hoopR)

Key Categories: Points, Rebounds, Assists, Steals, Blocks, and Personal Fouls.
Sample: Both leagues display 2,000 sampled individual game performances with linear regression trendlines calculated across all 12,013 games.

title: Story
text: As a basketball player and fan, I became interested in analyzing Women’s Basketball statistics. After comparing players across multiple seasons and researching reliable data sources, I discovered a positive correlation between minutes played and points, assists, steals, rebounds, and blocks. This inspired me to create a website using graphs and data to highlight player performance, celebrate their legacies, and showcase the growth of Women’s Basketball. I have also compared my data to Men’s Basketball to prove that women are just as capable as men.

title: Story
text:
About the Data
The datasets comprise 12,013 individual player-game box scores from the 2025–2026 regular seasons: - WNBA Data: Sourced via SportsDataverse (wehoop). - NBA Data: Sourced from ESPN via SportsDataverse (hoopR).
To ensure a balanced comparison across both leagues, each league’s sample contains 12,013 observations, with 2,000 performances plotted in each interactive visualization. The dashed trendlines represent linear regressions fitted across all 12,013 games.
